items.title: qa-evaluator custom subagent was not available as a subagent_type in a session that predated its creation
items.scope: verification only, no production code changes expected
items.reason: During Architecture V2 Shadow Trial #1 (docs/ARCHITECTURE_V2_EVALUATION_PLAN.md), invoking the Agent tool with subagent_type='qa-evaluator' (.claude/agents/qa-evaluator.md, added in the immediately prior task) failed with 'Agent type not found' -- worked around by having a general-purpose subagent read and follow that file's instructions directly. Root cause confirmed (not just suspected): custom subagent definitions load once at session start; both prior sessions (Trial #1 and Trial #2) were long-running sessions that started before/without a reload after the file existed in a state the harness's project-scan picked up. A genuinely fresh Claude Code v2.1.268 session in this repo lists qa-evaluator natively in its available-agent-types system reminder from the first turn.
items.evidence: Fresh-session probe (2026-09-11): Agent tool invoked with subagent_type='qa-evaluator' and a trivial read-only task ('report the latest V2 trial number without changing any files'). Result returned as a genuinely separate subagent context: it self-identified in its own reply as 'the qa-evaluator subagent' with the exact prescribed duty from .claude/agents/qa-evaluator.md, used only its allowed tools (Read/Grep, 4 tool_uses, 22186ms), and reported real findings (highest trial = Trial #2) with correct source citations. This is direct evidence of native separate-context execution, not a general-purpose fallback silently answering in the requested persona.
items.verification_required: DONE: native invocation confirmed live in a fresh session; the subagent's own self-reported identity plus tool-call telemetry is the proof.

items.title: Browser-level automated regression suite (Playwright) -- established as the project's new quality gate
items.reason: Owner directive: 'Owner manual review should verify product quality, not discover basic deterministic defects.' Smallest robust Playwright Test setup added -- resilient role/text/scoped-class locators, built-in auto-waiting/web-first assertions, no arbitrary sleeps. Usable locally (auto-starts the dev server via webServer config), against an already-running server, or as read-only smoke verification against production (PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL env var, never touches the local server in that mode). items.title: NEEDS_OWNER_DECISION: a real transient production 502/timeout was observed during independent QA, self-recovered, root cause not established
items.reason: The native qa-evaluator subagent, while independently verifying Phase 1+2 against production (2026-09-11), observed a real HTTP 502 Bad Gateway from Railway's own edge on /learn after a ~300s hang, followed by several minutes of request timeouts, with general internet connectivity confirmed fine throughout. Production self-recovered; an immediate rerun of curl, the Python suite, and the full Playwright suite all passed cleanly. Root cause NOT established -- plausibly an unrelated Railway platform event, OR the burst of ~13 concurrent Playwright browser sessions (used for this task's own verification) straining the backend. This is evidence worth the Owner's attention, not a contract failure (uptime/resilience under concurrent E2E load was not one of the stated acceptance criteria) and NOT something this autonomous task should decide how to address (could imply needing Railway plan changes, backend concurrency limits, or simply monitoring -- all business/infrastructure judgment calls).
items.evidence: qa-evaluator's own verification report (2026-09-11, task 'Independent QA of Phase 1+2 fixes') -- observed via direct curl against the real production edge, includes response headers (server: railway-hikari, x-railway-edge: ams1).
items.verification_required: Owner decision: investigate Railway logs around the observed timeframe, and/or decide whether to bound Playwright's local worker concurrency when it might run against production in the future (currently unbounded via playwright.config.js's default parallelism).

items.title: NEEDS_OWNER_DECISION: the deployed platform-backend container can never git-push to origin/GitHub (real, confirmed live, not guessed)
items.reason: JOB-SEARCH P0 (2026-09-12) added a required git-push step to the public trainer demo pipeline (a local commit is not durably saved). The FIRST real live production demo run (trainer-7e098fb3) proved every other stage genuinely works (investigation, apply, compile, testing-state, commit, deploy, independent production content verification) but push failed with "fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository". Root cause confirmed directly in the Dockerfile's own pre-existing, documented comment: this image deliberately `git init`s a fresh, disconnected local repository with no history/remote at all when none is uploaded (a decision made before push was a requirement, to fix an earlier real incident where the container had no usable git repo at all for `git commit`/`git rev-parse`). Fixing this for real requires the deployed container to have a configured `origin` remote with WRITE credentials (a GitHub PAT or deploy key) -- provisioning that is a secrets/architecture decision this task deliberately did NOT make unilaterally, per this project's own policy that writing secrets/changing deploy architecture requires explicit Owner approval, not autonomous action.
items.evidence: Real live run trainer-7e098fb3 (2026-09-12) push event: {"ok": false, "output": "fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository..."}. Dockerfile lines ~63-77 (search "ROOT CAUSE") document the deliberate disconnected-repo decision this predates. The run still reached COMPLETED (push failure is non-fatal by design -- Railway deploys from the local working tree, not GitHub), and the requested production content change was independently verified live regardless.
items.verification_required: Owner decision: either (a) provision a GitHub PAT/deploy key as a Railway secret and wire `git remote add origin` + credential injection into the Dockerfile/container startup (a real secrets + architecture change), or (b) accept that trainer-demo commits only ever exist in the deployed container's ephemeral local repo (lost on next redeploy) and that only a local developer/Claude Code session's own push keeps canonical history in sync with what a live demo actually shipped -- and update the Workbench's own "Push" UI copy to state this honestly rather than implying full durability today.

items.title: Real backend/API demo (e.g. the customer-not-found 404 message) is currently unverifiable by the trainer pipeline's existing content check -- deliberately not attempted live
items.scope: agent/web_server.py's _run_trainer_thread VERIFYING PRODUCTION step (_fetch_public_app + trainer_expected_content substring check)
items.reason: JOB-SEARCH P0 (2026-09-12) asked for a second, bounded backend demo (the Customer App's 404 message) in addition to the UI demo. Inspection before attempting it found a structural gap: production verification currently checks whether `edit.new_content` (the ENTIRE new file's source text) appears as a substring of the Customer App's ROOT PAGE HTML -- which only works by coincidence for a static HTML file (the file IS what gets served) and is meaningless for a compiled Java change, since a deployed JAR never echoes its own Java source in any HTTP response, and the root page is not even the right endpoint to check for a controller-level message change. Attempting a real backend demo without fixing this first would either produce a false DEPLOYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN/FAILED for a genuinely correct change, or require rushing an unverified new verification subsystem into a real production deploy under time pressure -- both explicitly against this task's own instruction ('Do not fabricate success' / 'choose a safer bounded backend example' when a mutation would introduce unsafe/unverifiable state).
items.evidence: Direct code inspection of _fetch_public_app() (only ever fetches PUBLIC_CUSTOMER_APP_URL's root page) and _run_trainer_thread's content_verified check (run.trainer_expected_content in after_html) -- confirmed this is the only production-verification mechanism that exists today. The real UI demo (trainer-7e098fb3) exercised this path successfully because a static HTML change's own new content genuinely is what the root page serves.
items.verification_required: A future task: design a real verification mechanism for non-static changes (e.g., derive the actual requested-effect assertion from a diff of old_content/new_content plus a designated endpoint to check, rather than a whole-file substring match against the wrong page) BEFORE attempting a live backend demo against the real Customer App -- then run it for real, with the same independent-production-verification discipline the UI demo used.
